Simulation-based infit MSQ cutoffs for multiply imputed data

Source: R/infit_cutoff_mi.R
RMitemInfitCutoffMI.Rd

The counterpart of RMitemInfitCutoff() for data imputed with the mice package. Runs the simulations in each imputed dataset and stacks them, so that the interval per item reflects both sampling variability and the uncertainty from imputation. The result is used by RMitemInfitMI().

Usage

RMitemInfitCutoffMI(
  mids_object,
  iterations = 500,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  cutoff_method = "hdci",
  hdci_width = 0.999
)

Arguments

mids_object

A mids object from mice::mice(). Each completed dataset must contain only the item response columns, with no ID or grouping variables. Items are scored from 0. Items imputed as factors, as the polr method needs, are converted back to numbers. Their levels must be the response codes ("0", "1", ...).

iterations

Integer. Total number of simulated datasets across all imputations, split about evenly between the m imputed datasets, so at least m. Default 500. See the section on interval width.

parallel

Logical. Run the simulations within each imputed dataset in parallel via mirai. Default TRUE. Passed to RMitemInfitCutoff().

n_cores

Integer or NULL. Number of parallel workers. Passed to RMitemInfitCutoff.

verbose

Logical. Show progress messages (default FALSE).

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility, from which a seed for each imputation is derived. See easyRasch2-reproducibility for what this guarantees and how it interacts with parallel.

cutoff_method

Character. How the interval per item is computed from the stacked simulations: "hdci" (default), the highest-density continuous interval from ggdist::hdci() (needs ggdist), or "quantile", the 2.5th to 97.5th percentiles.

hdci_width

Numeric. Width of the interval with cutoff_method = "hdci". Default 0.999, see the section on interval width. Ignored with "quantile".

Value

A list like that of RMitemInfitCutoff(), which RMitemInfitMI() and RMitemInfitPlot() accept, with:

results

data.frame with the columns iteration, imputation, Item, InfitMSQ and OutfitMSQ, the stacked simulations from all imputed datasets.

item_cutoffs

data.frame with per-item cutoff summaries: Item, infit_low, infit_high, outfit_low, outfit_high. Computed from the stacked distribution.

actual_iterations

Total number of successful iterations across all imputations.

requested_iterations

The iterations requested.

sample_n

Number of rows (respondents) per imputed dataset.

sample_n_total, sample_has_na

As in RMitemInfitCutoff(): sample_n and FALSE, since imputed datasets drop no one.

sample_summary

Summary statistics of estimated person parameters from the first imputed dataset.

item_names

Character vector of item names.

cutoff_method

The method used to compute cutoffs.

hdci_width

The HDCI width used.

n_imputations

Number of imputed datasets used.

iterations_per_imputation

Integer vector of requested iterations per imputed dataset.

actual_iterations_per_imputation

Integer vector of successful iterations per imputed dataset.

dgp

"resample", the data-generating process used in each imputed dataset.

Details

Each of the m imputed datasets is completed with mice::complete() and passed to RMitemInfitCutoff(), with ceiling(iterations / m) or floor(iterations / m) iterations each. The simulations from all imputations are stacked, and the interval per item is computed from the stack.

Imputed datasets in which the model cannot be fitted are dropped with a warning. If all imputations fail, the function stops with an error.

The mice package must be installed (it is in Suggests).

Interval width under multiple imputation

hdci_width defaults to 0.999 here, not to the 0.95 of RMitemInfitCutoff(). RMitemInfitMI() has no corrected p-value yet, so under imputation the interval is still the decision rule, and it keeps a width chosen for that. Its family-wise error rate is 1 - 0.999^k over k items. An interval this wide needs roughly 5000 iterations in all before it reaches its stated width (Johansson, 2026). Combining bootstrap p-values across imputations is planned but needs its own calibration, since Johansson (2026) covers complete data only.

References

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

See also

RMitemInfitMI() for the pooled test, RMitemInfitPlot() to plot the simulated values, RMitemInfitCutoff() for complete data.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("mice", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("iarm", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Create example data with ~10% MCAR missingness
  set.seed(42)
  mat <- matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 8, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 8)
  mat[sample(length(mat), round(0.10 * length(mat)))] <- NA
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(mat)
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:8)

  # mice's ordinal method (`polr`) requires the items to be ordered
  # factors, so code them as such before imputing. RMitemInfitCutoffMI()
  # converts the completed factors back to numeric internally.
  sim_data[] <- lapply(sim_data, function(x) factor(x, ordered = TRUE))

  # Impute (use more imputations, e.g. m = 5+, in real analyses)
  imp <- mice::mice(sim_data, m = 2, method = "polr", seed = 123,
                    printFlag = FALSE)

  # Simulation-based cutoffs across imputations (use far more
  # iterations in real analyses, see the section on interval width)
  cutoff_mi <- RMitemInfitCutoffMI(imp, iterations = 50, parallel = FALSE,
                                seed = 42)
  cutoff_mi$item_cutoffs

  # Use with RMitemInfitMI()
  RMitemInfitMI(imp, cutoff = cutoff_mi)
}
#> 
#> 
#> Table: Pooled MSQ values from 2 imputations (Rubin's rules). n = 200 respondents (missing values imputed, m = 2) per imputed dataset. Cutoff values based on 50 total simulation iterations across 2 imputations (99.9% HDCI). Flagged: overfit = infit below range; underfit = above range.
